height.title: What happened in the air
height.hint: Phases are detected automatically from motor use and climb rate.

height.sinkNote: Glide sink rate comes straight from the vario: the model's own sinking speed plus any rising or sinking air. Over many flights the typical value approximates your model's sink rate. A true glide ratio needs an airspeed or GPS sensor.

path.noGpsTitle: No GPS in this log, so no map
path.noGpsText: Map, distance and speed need a GPS sensor. Without one we only know the height, not where the model was. A path guessed from the rotation sensors would drift by tens of metres within seconds, so it is not shown.
path.rotationTitle: What the rotation sensors can tell
path.periods: {n, plural, one {# circling period} other {# circling periods}}
path.directionNote: Left or right is not yet verified for this receiver installation.
path.circlingNote: Circles are counted from the pitch and yaw rotation sensors, which together measure how fast the model turns. Circling while climbing with the motor off is the classic sign of a thermal.
path.shadowHint: The path projected onto the ground, to see where the model was over the terrain.
path.follow: Height · move here to follow the model
path.followThrottle: Throttle · move here to follow the model

batteries.title: Batteries
batteries.hint: Smart batteries report their own ID and charge cycles, so every session can be linked to the pack that powered it.
batteries.naming: Batteries are named A, B, … in order of first use in the loaded files. Give them your own names, ideally the one written on the pack: names stay with the battery's ID in every file.
batteries.stuckHint: Sent frozen cell voltages at least once. Possibly a faulty pack.
batteries.partialHint: Identifies itself but never sends cell voltages.
batteries.unknownHint: No smart-battery data. Possibly a pack that stopped reporting, or a battery without telemetry.
batteries.none: No smart batteries in the loaded files.
batteries.note: Condition compares the voltage drop under load between flights. A pack whose drop keeps growing is wearing out.
batteries.ageingNote: internal resistance per cell, one dot per flight
batteries.ageingNotEnough: A trend needs at least 5 flights over 2 weeks. So far: {points, plural, one {# flight} other {# flights}} over {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
batteries.ageingRetire: Has reached the retire level of 15 mΩ per cell.
batteries.ageingForecast: Reaches the retire level of 15 mΩ per cell in about {n} charge cycles at this rate.
batteries.ageingStable: No wear worth noting: the resistance is not heading for the retire level.
batteries.ageingNow: Now {now} mΩ per cell, {change} mΩ per 10 charge cycles (trend over the last 10 flights).
batteries.ageingCold: Hollow dots are flights below {t}. Cold packs read high, so they are left out of the trend.
batteries.noneForModel: No smart batteries in the flights of this model.
batteries.namingGrouped: Batteries are named A, B, … in order of first use in the loaded files, and listed under the model each flew most often. Give them your own names, ideally the one written on the pack: names stay with the battery's ID in every file.

help.title: Who can use TLMscope
help.intro: TLMscope shows what happened during your flights. It reads the telemetry logs (.TLM files) that Spektrum transmitters save, and turns them into flight summaries, charts and simple ratings.
help.youCan: You can use it if you fly a model with a Spektrum telemetry receiver and your Spektrum transmitter saves telemetry logs.
help.r1w: Internal storage: Model.TLM and the AutoLog folder. Copy via USB.
help.r3: Spektrum DX6 G2/G3, DX7 G2, DX8 G2, DX9, DX10t, DX18 (G2 and later), DX18t, DX20
help.r3w: SD card, once telemetry logging is switched on.
help.whatYouSee: What you can see, and what it needs
help.whatHint: A log only contains what the sensors in your model sent. Missing hardware means missing data, not an error.
help.d1: Radio link: frame losses, holds, fades, receiver voltage, signal strength
help.d1n: Any Spektrum telemetry receiver (model names ending in “T”)
help.d2: Motor, controller and BEC: rpm, current, voltage, throttle, temperatures
help.d3: Battery: cell voltages, temperature, ID, charge cycles, capacity
help.d3n: Spektrum Smart battery, connected through a Smart ESC
help.d4n: Vario / altimeter sensor, or a receiver that reports it
help.d9: Other sensors (airspeed, extra current or temperature sensors, …)

st.exp: Expected to work, not tested yet
st.spec: Built from the specification, not tested yet
st.raw: Shown as raw data for now
st.gps: Tested with one real GPS log

help.n1: EdgeTX / OpenTX logs (CSV, e.g. RadioMaster, FrSky, ExpressLRS, Crossfire): planned, not available yet.
help.n2: Other radio systems with their own log formats (Jeti, Graupner HoTT, Futaba, Multiplex …).
help.n3: Flight controller logs (ArduPilot, Betaflight blackbox, iNav).
help.n4: Spektrum transmitters that cannot save telemetry logs (e.g. DX6i).
help.n5: Live telemetry during the flight. TLMscope works with the saved files afterwards.
help.n6: Changing settings on the transmitter or receiver. TLMscope only reads.
help.n7: Cars and boats (Spektrum surface radios) are not a focus. Their logs may partly work.
help.privateText: Files are read in your browser and never uploaded. There is no account, no cookies and no server that stores your data. Only anonymous page views are counted (Umami, without cookies and without anything from your files). One exception: for logs with GPS, the map on the <mapLink>Flight path</mapLink> tab loads map images from OpenFreeMap (tiles.openfreemap.org). Like any website, that service sees your IP address and which map area is requested, so roughly where the flight was. Your log file itself is not sent.
help.offlineText: After one visit with internet, TLMscope is stored in your browser and also opens without a connection, for example at the flying field. Once it is ready, the footer says “Works offline”. On iPhone and iPad, add it to the home screen, otherwise Safari deletes it after some days without use. Only the map needs internet.
help.getLogs: How to get your log files
help.g1: NX and iX: connect the transmitter by USB, choose the option to access internal storage in the USB settings, then copy the .TLM files.
help.g2: DX with SD card: take the SD card out and copy the .TLM files.
help.independent: TLMscope is an independent project, not made or endorsed by Spektrum or Horizon Hobby.
help.aboutText: TLMscope is made by {name}. It started as a way to understand my own RC flights better than the transmitter screen allows. It is free, has no ads, and the source code is open. Ideas, questions and bug reports are welcome on GitHub.
